title: fix(compiler-vapor): do not fold a constant prop with no content attribute
body:
`<video :volume="0.5">` prints `volume="0.5"` into the markup and leaves `el.volume` at `1`, where VDOM sets the property - at runtime the rule is `key in el`, and a property that has no content attribute cannot survive a trip through the element's template string. A static literal binding is folded into that string, so the write is simply lost. The same holds for `playbackRate`, `defaultPlaybackRate`, `currentTime` and `valueAsNumber`, and since HTML parsing lowercases the key, what is left behind is `playbackrate="2"`.

[playground](https://play.vuejs.org/#) - two children render the same `<video :volume="0.5">`, one compiled as Vapor and one as VDOM. Look at the two lines: VDOM reports `el.volume = 0.5` with clean markup, Vapor reports `el.volume = 1` and a stray `volume="0.5"` in the markup.

`dynamicKeys` exists for exactly this class and already carries `indeterminate`, so these keys join it. The list approximates `key in el`, which the compiler cannot evaluate, and does not try to be exhaustive - the comment says as much, and a key it misses is still reachable with `.prop`. Keys whose attribute does feed the property keep folding, `muted` among them, since the parser initializes the muted state from the attribute; control tests pin that. Two notes: this is the client render only - after hydration both renderers leave the property at its default, so they stay in step - and where a value is invalid Vapor now emits the same `Failed setting prop` warning VDOM already did.
